NDIA-ICT-SVM-001
1. Service governance, portfolio and value
Service governance, portfolio, value and performance

NDIA must govern each ICT service through a defined owner, delegated decision rights, service purpose, portfolio roadmap, transition approval, performance measures and benefits evidence that support executive, Board and whole-of-government reporting.
Applies to all ICT services, service proposals, major changes, operational transitions and portfolio reporting.

2. Risk, assurance and integrity controls
Risk management, assurance, internal control and fraud prevention

ICT service risks, including security, shared, supplier, residual, fraud and corruption risks, must be identified, assessed, assigned, treated, tested, monitored and reported within NDIA risk appetite, with exceptions and control gaps formally accepted and tracked.
Applies across service strategy, design, change, release, operation, supplier management and retirement.

4. Information protection, privacy and lawful handling
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure

ICT services must protect classified, caveated, protected, personal and critical infrastructure information by applying lawful collection, access, use, disclosure, sharing, privacy governance, PIA, metadata, consent, security and disposal controls.
Applies where services collect, store, process, use, disclose, share, publish, transfer or dispose of sensitive or regulated information.

5. Records, knowledge and evidence lifecycle
Records, knowledge, FOI, publication, retention and evidence management

ICT service records, knowledge articles, CMDB data, service decisions, FOI material, publication content and archival records must be accurate, searchable, secure, accessible, retained, transferred or disposed of only under approved records and information management controls.
Applies to ITSM tools, knowledge bases, service catalogues, operational records, FOI/IPS publication processes, migrations and decommissioning.

Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance

Applies to ICT procurements, contracts, outsourced services, managed services, subcontractors, supplier onboarding, reviews and exits.

Applies to new services, material changes, releases, operational acceptance, asset/configuration updates and service retirement.

Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration

Applies to all services, applications, operating systems, devices, vulnerabilities, security exceptions and cyber control changes.

AI governance, transparency, training, lifecycle controls and impact assessment

Applies where an ICT service uses, integrates, procures, operates or supports an AI system or AI-enabled feature.
